note:
[Balanced Budget @ C48] Reduced to 226,077.79 | justification: Restored in Tier 1- This reduction eliminates the position of Young Adult Services Librarian, a 30 hr./week employee.  The community would lose a key professional librarian role (1 of 5 Master’s-level librarians) who works with the important young adult demographic. The loss would be especially impactful shortly after town leaders committed a significant amount of capital to improving the Teen Room with more than $120,000 from ARPA funds. The reduction also decreases staff availability for absence coverage to meet operational safety requirements.   The library will need to eliminate structured after-school activities and Teen Advisory Board volunteer opportunities. Additionally, the community will see reduced quality and frequency of Summer Reading Program for Young Adults, book displays and collection maintenance, and outreach and partnerships.  
Operational impact will include increased strain on remaining staff to cover evening shifts, potential scheduling gaps, negative impact on staff morale and increased difficulty to retain staff talent. To partially counter the morale and retention impact, the library might close one evening per week, but this reduces community access by 25% for evening space use, creating significant impacts on local groups such as Scouts, and would result in lost shifts for one Library Page. Other impacts will be less immediately visible but will reduce teen-focused programming and increase reliance on outside funding sources.  The Young Adult Services Librarian represents 11% of total staff hours and plays a critical role in supporting teen engagement, literacy, and safe after-school space. Reduced staffing and resources will directly affect service quality, accessibility, and the overall user experience for the community.

If this line were not funded, the Recreation Director position would be eliminated, along with most organized recreation programming provided by the Town. Under Tier 2, the position is funded at a full-time level, which has been discussed in prior years as a way to expand programming, improve coordination of park and field use, and provide more consistent year-round recreation services.

The position is responsible for coordinating recreation programming for the community, including summer sports camps, STEM and after-school programs, parks and recreation billing, management of beach staff and seasonal operations, and scheduling and oversight of field and park rentals.  If this line were not funded, the Recreation Director position would be eliminated, along with most organized recreation programming provided by the Town. This would affect after-school and summer programs that are widely used by families, and the associated administrative duties would need to be reassigned. In particular, billing and scheduling functions related to parks and field use would likely shift to existing facilities administrative staff, increasing workload in that office.  Under Tier 1, funding restores the position at its current level, allowing recreation programming and related services to continue. Under Tier 2, the position is funded at a full-time level, which has been discussed in prior years as a way to expand programming, improve coordination of park and field use, and provide more consistent year-round recreation services.

note: [Balanced Budget @ C54] Reduced to 60,000 | justification: Increased in Tier 1- This line is reduced from FY26 level funding of $70,000 in the balanced budget and is increased in Tier 1.  This line item covers all maintenance and repair to the town parks and fields. The primary users of these fields are the Lunenburg Schools baseball and softball programs, the Lunenburg youth baseball and softball league as well as a couple of rentals for various leagues.  The reduction to this line item will limit us to regular maintenance only such as mowing at a reduced frequency, seasonal clean up activities and some infield maintenance. This will also leave the parks department with minimal unforeseen repair money and no money for improvements such as fence repairs, field repairs, improvements to parking areas and repairs to structures. This is a line the facilities and parks department has been trying to increase for the last few years in an attempt to tackle some of the deferred maintenance on all of parks locations.
